text:
I have been living in Thailand for several months. This is the first time I have felt so angry about a service experience.

Today, I went to pick up my tailored tooth retainers. I asked the receptionist whether they had been cleaned, and she replied that they had already been cleaned. After that, I put them in my mouth. Immediately, a strong bitter taste spread across my tongue, and I started vomiting.

I went to the restroom and washed the retainers myself, but it did not help. I continued vomiting and felt extremely uncomfortable. During this time, none of the nurses or receptionists asked whether I was okay or offered any assistance. I showed them the blue chemical residue on the retainers, but they did not seem to know what to do.

Later, an elderly lady approached me and said, “You need to wash it by yourself.” I replied, “I already washed it.” Eventually, another dentist came and helped me clean the retainers using a different type of solution, after which the bitter taste finally disappeared.

Up to now, I still do not know what those blue chemical residues were or whether they are harmful to my health. After this incident, I began to question whether the politeness and humble image of Thai people is sometimes only superficial. When a patient is vomiting, shouldn’t medical staff at least ask if the patient is okay?

When I queried this about the price sign standing on the counter stating 800 baht for a filling and why she was trying to charge for two she just kept ignoring me and trying to carry on until I got up and went and got the price list, whilst also asking why she was charging for two teeth.
